title: Release notes — Chrome for Developers
why_trusted: Google's own Chrome for Developers release-notes index, which states that release notes from Chrome 155 onward live on Chrome Platform Status and links the stable and beta channels plus the site RSS feed.

title: Frontend Mentor — practice challenges for front-end developers
why_trusted: The practice platform's own site, which states that 1,207,602 people build portfolio-worthy projects there and publishes 133 challenges in five difficulty levels with design files, a product-spec format, and a code review loop.

title: Getting started with MDN Web Docs
why_trusted: Mozilla's own contribution guide for MDN Web Docs, the reference documentation of the web platform, which defines the public loop of picking a task, opening a pull request, and getting reviewed writing.

title: Learn web development
why_trusted: MDN's own learning area: the structured tutorial path that Mozilla maintains for front-end skills, and the page that states its module order, its skill tests and its build challenges.

title: The web standards model
why_trusted: MDN's own account of which bodies write the web standards (W3C, WHATWG, TC39 with ECMA, Khronos) and how a feature moves from explainer to specification, so a learner can reach the primary source instead of a tutorial summary.

title: Baseline
why_trusted: The official hub for the Baseline browser-support status, published on the Chrome team's own site; the page states that Baseline was originated by the Chrome team and is now defined by the WebDX Community Group.

title: Implementing feature detection
why_trusted: MDN's guide to feature detection: the canonical statement that a browser test must check for the feature and never for the browser name, with @supports and CSS.supports() as the native mechanisms.

title: ai/nanoid: A tiny (118 bytes), secure, URL-friendly, unique string ID generator for JavaScript
why_trusted: The original Nano ID implementation, written by the library's author and built by Evil Martians, MIT licensed, and shipped as a runtime dependency of Vite ("nanoid": "^5.1.16" in packages/vite/package.json) and of PostCSS ("nanoid": "^3.3.20" in postcss/package.json).

title: pmndrs/zustand: Bear necessities for state management in React
why_trusted: The organisation-owned reference implementation of a modern React store, MIT licensed with eight CI workflows and a vitest suite, and a runtime dependency of cal.com ("zustand": "4.5.2" in packages/features/package.json) and of OpenReplay's tracker package ("zustand": "^4.5.2" in tracker/tracker-zustand/package.json).
